assignments.brief_reason: Sets a high removal threshold for extreme demeaning/hate-adjacent content while tolerating insensitive language.
Claims the posts didn’t influence them, framed as a low-influence decision.
Uses First Amendment rights framing with a harm-based boundary for removal, aligning with free-speech thresholds.
Believes moderation isn’t needed because content is ordinary opinions/exaggeration, implying permissive speech boundaries.
Uses a harm/toxicity-adjacent threshold (good faith vs angry/violent rhetoric) to decide removal.
Opposes removal to avoid silencing viewpoints, fitting a free-speech boundary logic.
Notes mirror similarity makes the joint decision easy, indicating pair comparisons barely influenced decisions.
Applies free-speech bounds with intent/maliciousness and disallows crossing into hate speech or misinformation.
Explicitly ignores political pair contrast and bases decisions on other criteria, indicating low pair influence.
Says the opposing views didn’t change perceived intent; relies on checks rather than pair-driven influence.
Removal is limited to content viewed as unhealthy/angry/violent, which functions as a harm/toxicity threshold.
Uses the pair to check for truth across sides, which doesn’t match the provided harm-threshold or low-influence themes directly.
Focuses on meta-process neutrality and bias mitigation rather than explicit harm thresholds or lack of pair influence.
States a neutrality goal (stay neutral) without clear mapping to harm thresholds or pair-ineffectiveness.
Absolutist First Amendment stance with removal only when harm/threat is present.
Allows speech unless it appears to be a threat or act of violence, using harm-based permissive logic.
Tolerates swearing unless used harmfully/directed at others—an explicit toxicity/manner threshold.
Aims for balance across far-reaching viewpoints, not clearly about harm thresholds or pair influence.
Removes when foul language targets/attacks someone, reflecting a toxicity/harassment threshold.
States their decision was not really influenced and relies on an opinions-entitlement norm, indicating minimal pair influence.
